title: Configure editor and type checks
objective: Distinguish a typed practice model from real editor and compiler settings.
tasks: Enable formatOnSave and strict with boolean true values in /project.ts.
Confirm exactly two of the four practice checks are ready.
In your own editor, enable editor.formatOnSave and inspect compilerOptions.strict in the exported tsconfig.json.
hints: The strings "true" and "false" are not boolean values.
Editing this model changes the checklist; it does not reconfigure VS Code or the sandbox compiler.

Practice on your own computer

This page does not execute terminal commands or change VS Code, Git, or TypeScript settings.

  1. Export the project, open it in VS Code, and enable editor.formatOnSave in your editor settings.
  2. Open a real terminal: run git init and then git status.
  3. Inspect the exported tsconfig.json and its strict setting, then run pnpm install and pnpm exec tsc --noEmit.
  4. Run pnpm exec vite --host 0.0.0.0 to start the real development server.

title: Use scripts and a Git checkpoint
objective: Finish the script model, then practice a real local tool workflow.
tasks: Set scripts.dev to vite --host 0.0.0.0 and scripts.typecheck to tsc --noEmit in /project.ts.
Confirm all four checklist items are ready; these values are still only practice data.
Export the project, install dependencies, run pnpm exec tsc --noEmit and pnpm dev in a real terminal, then stop the server with Ctrl+C.
In your own new project folder, run git init and git status; inspect the diff, stage your source files, and commit a working checkpoint.
hints: Use the exact script strings shown by the tasks.
The exported project already has a dev script. Add a real typecheck script to package.json if you want pnpm typecheck.
